first.rationale: Two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) both point to onboarding/signup simplification improving activation and time-to-value, directly addressing two of the three current problems (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) with a clean, non-flagged evidence base. I want to verify both source records because they overlap in claim (simplification vs shortening) and I need to confirm they're distinct enough experiments to be mutually reinforcing rather than the same result double-counted. I deliberately did not choose promotional_pricing despite the competitor threat: memory_73 carries an explicit caveat about pooled cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, making its acquisition/revenue lift numbers unreliable, and matching a competitor's aggressive entry pricing risks a race-to-the-bottom that could degrade long-term qualified revenue even if it produces short-term acquisition gains. With only one experiment slot this week, the onboarding fix is the more evidentially solid and lower-risk bet against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; the pricing question deserves a dedicated, cleanly-designed test later rather than a rushed reaction this week.
